title: OpenAI reveals Responses API, Agents SDK for building agentic experiences
summary: SD Times reports that OpenAI launched the Responses API, which combines Chat Completions with built-in tools (web search, file search, computer use), and the open-source Agents SDK, the successor to the experimental Swarm project. OpenAI says the SDK provides handoffs between agents, guardrails, and tracing, and works with third-party models that expose a Chat Completions-style endpoint; it launched Python-only. OpenAI also stated it plans to deprecate the Assistants API, with a sunset targeted for mid-2026.
relevance: SDK-level 'handoffs' are a framework-native delegation primitive, and the Assistants-to-Responses deprecation is a concrete forced intra-vendor migration that tests how portable agent state is.
search_query: OpenAI "New tools for building agents" Responses API Agents SDK March 2025
notes: Primary OpenAI post (openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/) returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch; secondary coverage used instead. Article was updated 2025-03-24.

title: Meet Kagent, Open Source Framework for AI Agents in Kubernetes
summary: The New Stack reports that Solo.io introduced kagent, an Apache 2.0 framework for building and running AI agents inside Kubernetes to automate configuration, troubleshooting, observability and network-security tasks. The article says kagent was built on Microsoft's AutoGen and integrates cloud-native tools through MCP, with initial tools for Argo, Helm, Istio and Kubernetes. Solo.io's Lin Sun said the company intended to donate the project to the CNCF.
relevance: kagent represents agents as Kubernetes-managed workloads, a hosting substrate that makes agent placement and relocation a cluster-scheduling question.
search_query: kagent CNCF sandbox Solo.io Kubernetes AI agents

title: Agent Development Kit: Making it easy to build multi-agent applications
summary: Google introduced the open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) at Cloud NEXT 2025 for building hierarchical multi-agent systems with delegation and Sequential/Parallel/Loop workflow agents. Google says ADK agents can be containerized and deployed to any container runtime or to the managed Vertex AI Agent Engine, use Gemini or other models via Model Garden and LiteLLM, consume MCP tools, and wrap agents built in LangGraph or CrewAI as tools.
relevance: ADK explicitly embeds foreign-framework agents as tools and separates the agent from its hosting runtime, two patterns central to cross-framework and cross-runtime movement.
search_query: Google Agent Development Kit ADK launch Cloud Next 2025 Agent Engine

title: Build 2025: Microsoft Charts Wider Path for AI Agents
summary: RCP Magazine reports that at Build 2025 Microsoft made Azure AI Foundry Agent Service generally available for single- and multi-agent deployments, citing use of MCP and A2A, built-in AgentOps tracing, and a catalog of 1,900+ models. Microsoft also put Entra Agent ID into public preview to apply Conditional Access, audit trails and lifecycle policies to agents, and previewed Copilot Studio multi-agent delegation across Microsoft 365, Azure AI and Fabric agents.
relevance: It shows a hyperscaler hosting service pairing open interop protocols (A2A/MCP) with a first-class agent identity directory, the combination needed for accountable cross-agent delegation.
search_query: Azure AI Foundry Agent Service general availability Build 2025 news article techcommunity
notes: News coverage only, per theme rules; no Azure resources or services were used.

title: Docker Brings Compose to the Agent Era: Building AI Agents is Now Easy
summary: Docker announced that a single compose.yaml can declare open models, agents and MCP tools and bring the whole agent stack up with 'docker compose up', with integrations for LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, Embabel, Vercel AI SDK, Spring AI and Agno. It also announced Docker Offload to run heavy models and containers in the cloud from the same workflow, deployment to Google Cloud Run via 'gcloud run compose up', and said Azure Container Apps support was in progress.
relevance: A framework-agnostic declarative deployment file that runs unchanged on a laptop, an offload cloud or a serverless target is a practical form of agent-stack relocation.
search_query: Docker Compose agents AI frameworks LangGraph CrewAI Google ADK announcement July 2025
notes: Page headline differs slightly from the browser tab title ('Docker Brings Compose to the AI Agent Era').

title: Introducing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Securely deploy and operate AI agents at any scale (preview)
summary: AWS previewed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a set of services (Runtime with session isolation, Memory, Observability, Identity, Gateway, Browser, Code Interpreter) for hosting agents built with any framework and any model. AWS names CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex and Strands Agents as examples, cites MCP and A2A, and uses OpenTelemetry for observability. The preview ran in four regions with free use until 2025-09-16.
relevance: A framework-agnostic managed runtime with separate memory and identity services decouples agent state and credentials from code, a precondition for moving agents onto or off a platform.
search_query: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore generally available announcement
notes: Page carries a later note (2025-10-13) that AgentCore became generally available.

title: Build and Distribute AI Agents and Workflows with cagent
summary: Docker introduced cagent, an open-source CLI that runs agents declared in a single YAML file (models, instructions, toolsets, sub-agents) without writing code. Agents can be pushed to and pulled from OCI registries such as Docker Hub and run directly by reference, tools are attached via MCP (including the Docker MCP Gateway), and models are swappable across providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and local Docker Model Runner.
relevance: Packaging an agent definition as an OCI artifact is a concrete 'agent container' format that lets an agent be distributed and re-instantiated on another machine.
search_query: Docker blog cagent introducing agent builder runtime 2025

title: Introducing Microsoft Agent Framework (Preview): Making AI Agents Simple for Every Developer
summary: Microsoft released a public preview of Microsoft Agent Framework, building on Semantic Kernel, AutoGen and Microsoft.Extensions.AI, with migration guidance for Semantic Kernel users. The .NET post describes sequential, concurrent, handoff and group-chat workflow patterns, MCP servers as tools, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and agents that accept any IChatClient so model providers can be swapped without code changes.
relevance: The consolidation of two frameworks into one forces a real cross-framework migration for existing Semantic Kernel and AutoGen agents, a natural case study for migration tooling.
search_query: "Introducing Microsoft Agent Framework" azure.microsoft.com blog October 2025
notes: The Azure blog announcement and Visual Studio Magazine coverage returned HTTP 403; the .NET DevBlogs primary post was used. The unification with SK/AutoGen is stated in the author's comment reply rather than the post body.

title: OpenAI launches AgentKit to help developers build and ship AI agents
summary: TechCrunch reports that Sam Altman announced AgentKit at OpenAI DevDay 2025, comprising Agent Builder (a visual workflow designer built on the Responses API), ChatKit (an embeddable chat UI), Evals for Agents (trace grading, datasets, prompt optimization), and a Connector Registry managed via an admin control panel. The article does not give pricing or a general-availability date.
relevance: A vendor-hosted visual agent builder raises lock-in questions because workflows are defined in a proprietary format tied to one API.
search_query: OpenAI AgentKit launch DevDay Agent Builder

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available
summary: AWS announced general availability of Bedrock AgentCore in nine regions. AgentCore Runtime added Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol support, all services gained VPC, PrivateLink, CloudFormation and tagging support, and Gateway can now front existing MCP servers with IAM as well as OAuth authorization. AWS says it works with CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Google ADK and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and with models inside or outside Bedrock.
relevance: Native A2A in a managed runtime plus support for third-party SDKs (including a competitor's) is direct evidence of hosting platforms competing on framework portability.
search_query: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore generally available announcement

title: Unleashing autonomous AI agents: Why Kubernetes needs a new standard for agent execution
summary: Google engineers announced Agent Sandbox, a formal Kubernetes SIG Apps subproject (kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox) defining Sandbox, SandboxTemplate and SandboxClaim custom resources for isolated agent execution, with pluggable gVisor or Kata Containers backends. The post says a warm-pool orchestrator cuts cold starts to under one second, a Python SDK is provided, and the project was to be launched at KubeCon Atlanta in November 2025.
relevance: A vendor-neutral Kubernetes API for agent execution environments gives agent runtimes a common, schedulable unit that could be relocated across clusters.
search_query: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox SIG Apps announcement KubeCon

title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
summary: The Linux Foundation formed the Agentic AI Foundation with three founding contributions: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, Block's goose agent framework, and OpenAI's AGENTS.md convention. Platinum members are AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI, with 18 gold and 23 silver members. The release claims AGENTS.md has been adopted by more than 60,000 open-source projects and agent frameworks, including Codex, Cursor, Devin, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Jules and VS Code.
relevance: Neutral governance of MCP and AGENTS.md makes the agent-to-tool layer and repository-level agent instructions shared conventions across tools rather than vendor-owned formats.
search_query: Agentic AI Foundation Linux Foundation AGENTS.md MCP goose announcement
notes: The 60,000-project adoption figure is the Linux Foundation's own claim.

title: Oracle adopts AG-UI protocol for Agent Spec
summary: CopilotKit announced that Oracle's Open Agent Specification (Agent Spec), a framework-agnostic declarative JSON format for agents, now works with the AG-UI agent-user interaction protocol. The post says Agent Spec definitions run on LangGraph, WayFlow and CrewAI, and that an AG-UI adapter lets the same definition stream to any AG-UI frontend, including CopilotKit, without rebuilding the UI per framework; a starter repo was published.
relevance: Pairing a portable agent definition format with a framework-neutral UI protocol lets an agent move between runtimes while keeping its user-facing contract stable.
search_query: Agent Spec AG-UI CopilotKit Oracle integration announcement
notes: Oracle's own 'Introducing Open Agent Specification' blog returned HTTP 403 (WebFetch and curl), and its publication date could not be confirmed, so it was not included as a separate item.

title: Running Agents on Kubernetes with Agent Sandbox
summary: The Kubernetes project described Agent Sandbox, still in development under SIG Apps, as a declarative API for singleton, stateful agent workloads that would otherwise require a StatefulSet of size one, a headless Service and a PVC per agent. The Sandbox CRD provides gVisor or Kata isolation, scale-to-zero for idle agents with resumption where they left off, and a stable hostname and network identity; a SandboxWarmPool extension hands pre-warmed pods to SandboxClaims to avoid about one second of cold start.
relevance: Suspend/resume of a stateful agent workspace with stable identity is the infrastructure primitive underlying checkpoint-based runtime relocation.
search_query: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox SIG Apps announcement KubeCon
notes: WebFetch returned only the introduction; full text was confirmed via curl of the same URL.

title: Microsoft Agent Framework Version 1.0
summary: Microsoft shipped Agent Framework 1.0 for .NET and Python with stable APIs and a long-term support commitment. The post says the graph-based workflow engine is stable with checkpointing and hydration so long-running processes survive interruptions, supports pause/resume and human-in-the-loop, adds migration assistants that analyse Semantic Kernel and AutoGen code, supports MCP tools and A2A (with A2A 1.0 'coming soon'), and offers preview hosting on Microsoft Foundry or Azure Durable Functions.
relevance: Built-in checkpoint/hydration plus automated migration from two predecessor frameworks addresses both runtime relocation and cross-framework migration in one release.
notes: News coverage only; no Azure services used.

title: Welcome to Google Cloud Next '26
summary: In an adapted Next '26 keynote transcript, Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian announced the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which folds Vertex AI model services into a platform organised around build, scale, govern and optimise. Google claims runtime improvements with sub-second cold starts, an Agent Identity giving each agent a cryptographic ID with auditable authorization policies, an Agent Gateway that enforces policy over MCP and A2A traffic, an Agent Registry of internal agents and tools, and a graph-based ADK.
relevance: A protocol-aware gateway plus per-agent cryptographic identity is the control point at which cross-agent delegation can be authorised and audited.
search_query: Google Cloud Next 2026 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Agent Engine announcement
notes: Secondary sources describe this as the successor to Vertex AI; the keynote post itself says Vertex AI services are brought into the platform.

title: AgentCore harness is now generally available
summary: AWS made generally available a managed agent harness in Bedrock AgentCore that runs the orchestration loop, executes tools, manages the context window, persists state across turns, recovers from failures and isolates each session with its own filesystem, shell and browser. AWS says agents are defined by configuration, providers can be switched mid-session without losing context, memory persists across sessions, and one CLI command exports the harness to Strands-based code, with Claude Agent SDK export listed as coming soon.
relevance: Mid-session model switching with preserved context and config-to-code export are explicit, vendor-supported forms of portable context and framework migration.
notes: Some secondary sources give 2026-06-18; the AWS What's New page states 2026-06-17.

title: The case for a cloud native agent harness
summary: In a CNCF member post, Stacklok CEO Craig McLuckie argues that desktop-style agent harnesses do not suit multi-session, governed, fault-tolerant operation, and that 'a monolith in a container is still a monolith'. He describes Stacklok's early open-source Mecatl, which separates the agent loop from clients, execution environments and tools, keeps session state in durable storage so a replacement worker resumes from the last persisted turn boundary (turn-level durability, not in-flight resumption), and proposes, as an unshipped draft, a SPIFFE trust domain with the delegation chain encoded in a JWT.
relevance: It names turn-boundary checkpointing and delegation-chain identity as the concrete mechanisms for moving a live agent session between workers and clients, and states their limits.
search_query: cncf.io blog 2026 cloud-native agent harness McLuckie Stacklok
notes: Found via The New Stack 'Road to KubeCon' column (2026-10-02, Bill Doerrfeld), which summarises this post. Mecatl and its claims are from its own vendor.
